items.snippet: 이재명 대통령의 국정 지지율이 긍정 평가 39%, 부정 평가 50%로 집계됐다. 한국갤럽이 10∼12일 전국 만 18세 이상 1002명을 대상으로 실시해 13일 발표한 여론조사(전화면접 방식, 95% 신뢰수준에 표본오차 ±3.1%포인트, 자세한 사항은 중앙선거여론조사심의위원회 홈페이지 참조)에서 이 대통령의 국정에 대한 평가는 이같이 나타났다. 지난주 조사에서는 긍정 평가 41%, 부정 평가 50%였다. 긍정 평가 이유는 ‘경제·민생’(19%), ‘외교’(17%), ‘소통’(9%), 부정 평가 이유는 ‘부동산 정책’(17%), ‘경제·민생’(15%), ‘도덕성 문제·본인 재판 회피’(12%) 순이었다. 정당 지지율은 민주당 39%, 국민의힘 26%로 집계됐다. 지난주 조사에서는 민주당 36%, 국민의힘 28%였다. 양당 격차는 9월 추석 이후...

items.snippet: 국민의힘 윤리위원회 위원이 무소속 한동훈 의원에 대한 제명 결정이 ‘조작’이라는 주장을 제기한 것과 관련해 당내 파열음이 커지고 있다. 친한(친한동훈)계 의원들이 징계 무효화 및 진상조사 요구를 이어가자 당 지도부는 “정말 나쁜 행태의 저급한 정치 공작”이라며 반격에 나섰다. 친한계 의원들은 13일 당 윤리위 황경성 위원이 한 의원의 제명 결정이 조작됐다고 주장한 것과 관련해 진상 조사를 촉구하며 국민의힘 장동혁 대표를 압박했다. 국민의힘 안상훈 의원은 이날 통화에서 한 의원의 징계에 대해 “원천적 무효”라며 “당 차원에서 징계가 어떤 식으로 이루어졌는지 제대로 된 진상조사가 있어야 할 것”이라고 했다. 그러면서 “중진들을 포함해 많은 의원들 사이에서 다 한 의원 없이는 총선을 치르기 힘들다는 공감대가 형성되어 있다”며 한 의원 복당 필요성도...

items.title: “스마트안경 못잡는 것 아냐?”... 다른 자격시험까지 불신 번져

items.title: 신고할 땐 안 주고… 숨진 다음날 유족에 스마트워치 준 경찰
items.snippet: 지난 10일 살해된 A(15)양의 가족에게 경찰은 사건 발생 이튿날 긴급 신고용 스마트워치 3대를 지급했다. A양을 살해한 진모(59)씨 등 가해자 측이 유족을 위협할 우려가 있다는 이유였다. 그러나 A양 아버지는 본지에 “정작 스마트워치가 필요했던 건 내가 아니라 딸이었다”며 “딸이 살아 있을 때 수차례 실종 신고를 해도 주지 않더니 이제 와서 무슨 소용이냐”고 했다. 그는 “경찰은 꼭 일이 터지고 나서야 뭔가를 하는 것 같다”고 했다.

items.title: 거위들의 가을 나들이
items.snippet: 12일 오후 전북 전주시 덕진구에서 흰 옷을 입은 조양환씨와 거위 12마리가 횡단보도를 건너고 있다. 4년 전부터 거위를 키우기 시작했다는 조씨는 원래 인적 드문 밤에만 거위들과 산책에 나섰으나, 시민들이 거위를 보며 좋아하는 모습을 보고 하루 두 번 아침과 오후에 산책을 하게 됐다고 한다.

items.title: 경찰 ‘반포 아파트 부정청약 의혹’ 이혜훈 송치
items.snippet: 서울경찰청 광역수사단 금융범죄수사대는 13일 아파트 부정 청약 의혹을 받고 있는 이혜훈 전 의원을 사기·업무방해 등 혐의를 적용, 기소의견으로 공소청에 송치했다. 앞서 경찰은 이 전 의원이 당첨된 서울 반포동 원펜타스 아파트에 대해 몰수·보전(처분 금지) 신청했으나 법원 결정은 아직 나오지 않았다.

items.title: 올해 마지막 단풍일까… 오늘 전국 곳곳 비소식
items.snippet: 13일 대전 동구 ‘상소동 산림욕장’이 노랗고 붉은 단풍으로 물들었다. 시민들이 산책로를 걸으며 가을 정취를 즐기고 있다. 하늘에서 내려다본 모습이다. 기상청은 토요일인 14일 전국 곳곳에 비가 내리다가 밤에 대부분 그칠 것이라고 예보했다.

items.title: 대한외과학회 박도중 이사장·신응진 회장
items.snippet: 대한외과학회 신임 이사장에 박도중 서울대병원 위장관외과 교수, 신임 회장에 신응진 순천향대 부천병원 대장항문외과 교수가 취임했다. 임기는 각각 2년과 1년.

items.title: [부음] 김수옥 별세 외
items.snippet: ▲ 김수옥 별세, 손미자 · 손경식 강원CBS 대표· 손경희 모친상, 유효숙 강원도 여성정책팀장 시모상=13일10시9분 춘천호반병원, 발인 16일6시30분, (033)252-0046 ▲ 정무성 현대차 정몽구 재단 이사장 별세, 정주연 남편상, 정지영 · 정지윤 부친상=13일11시35분 서울아산병원, 발인 15일9시, (02)3010-2000

items.title: [오늘의 날씨] 2026년 11월 14일
‘월아산 숲속의 진주’ 대한민국 조경대상 대통령상
items.snippet: 경남 진주시의 산림복지시설인 ‘월아산 숲속의 진주’가 13일 국토교통부와 환경조경발전재단이 공동 주최한 제16회 대한민국 조경대상에서 대통령상을 수상했다. 오른쪽은 조규일 진주시장, 왼쪽은 박지홍 국토부 국토도시실장.

items.title: 서양 사람은 정말 술안주 안 먹나
items.snippet: “서양 사람들은 술 마실 때 안주를 안 먹나요?” 술 강의를 나가면 거의 빠지지 않고 받는 질문이다. 영화나 드라마 속 미국·영국·프랑스·독일인은 바에서 위스키나 칵테일 한 잔을 들고 서서 이야기만 나눈다. 테이블 가득 안주를 깔아 놓는 우리 술자리와는 사뭇 다르다.

items.title: 억울한 사람 구하라고 만든 법, 입 막는 데 쓰여서야
items.snippet: 2018년 3월 새벽, 뮤지컬 배우 강은일은 서울의 한 순댓국집에서 지인과 지인의 고교동창 A씨 등 다수와 술자리를 갖는다. 하지만 그 자리는 강씨에게 몇 년에 걸친 엄청난 비극의 서막이 되고 만다. A의 성범죄 무고로 피해를 본 것이다. A의 주장에 따르면 그날 강씨는 화장실에 들어간 A의 허리를 한 손으로 감싼 뒤 다른 한 손으로 가슴을 만지며 강제로 입맞춤했단다. 이 음식점 화장실은 출입문을 열고 들어가면 왼쪽은 여자, 오른쪽은 남자 칸으로 나뉘어 있고 가운데 세면대가 있는 구조였다. 강씨는 자신이 용변을 보고 세면대에서 손을 씻는데 A가 다짜고짜 스킨십을 했다고 반박한다. A를 바로 밀쳐냈지만, 그녀는 강씨에게 “가족관계는 어떻게 되냐” “집에 돈 많냐” 등 이상한 질문을 했다는 것이다. 일행이 화장실에 와서 두 사람을 떼어냈고 사건이...

items.title: 성수동 다음은 서촌·북촌?
items.snippet: 이탈리아 명품 브랜드 보테가 베네타가 팬진(fanzine·브랜드가 직접 발행하는 소규모 잡지) 공개 행사를 서울 서촌 ‘카멜커피’에서 지난 1일까지 보름가량 열었다. 유명 사진작가 유르겐 텔러가 보테가 베네타의 겨울 컬렉션 창작 과정을 포착·기록한 이미지로 꾸민 카페에는 행사 기간 내내 인파가 몰렸다. 매일 선착순 100명에게 나눠준 에코백을 받으려고 이른 새벽부터 길게 줄이 늘어서는 ‘오픈런’이 벌어지기도 했다. 성수동이나 청담동, 대형 백화점에서 주로 열리던 글로벌 명품 브랜드 이벤트가 경복궁을 마주한 로컬 카페에서 열린 것이다. 서촌과 북촌이 서울을 대표하는 새로운 트렌드 중심지로 자리매김하고 있음을 보여주는 상징적인 장면으로 받아들여지고 있다.

items.title: 분노 사회
items.snippet: 얼마 전 층간 소음으로 인한 다툼으로 이웃을 살해한 사건이 발생했습니다. 순간의 분노를 조절하지 못하고 행한 이와 유사한 사건이 빈번하게 발생하고 있습니다. 이로 인해 행위자가 받게 될 중한 처벌과 상대방이 입은 끔찍한 피해, 그리고 양쪽 가족들이 겪을 고통을 생각하면 참으로 안타깝습니다. 최근에는 분노한 나머지 복수할 목적으로 제3자에게 테러를 의뢰하고, 제3자는 돈을 받고 테러를 대행해주는 기상천외의 범죄까지 등장했습니다. 또한, 마치 사설 구난차가 사고 현장에 빠르게 도착해서 이득을 얻는 것처럼 사회적 분노를 일으킬 만한 타인의 행적을 찾아내어 인터넷에 영상의 형태로 공론화해서 이득(조회 수, 광고 수익 등)을 챙기는, 이른바 사이버 렉카도 늘어나고 있습니다. 이처럼 분노가 적절히 조절되지 못해 불행한 사태가 생기고, 타인의 분노를 이용...

items.title: 자연의 부패를 극복한 최고 발명품, ‘냉장 문명’이 녹아내린다면
items.snippet: 새벽 3시 서울 아파트 현관 앞으로 배송된 마트 보랭(保冷) 상자. 아르헨티나산 오징어, 호주 쇠고기, 노르웨이 고등어, 태국 계란, 페루 아보카도, 이탈리아 치즈, 중국 백합, 뉴질랜드 키위와 플로리다 오렌지가 은빛 보랭 포장재에 드라이아이스·얼음팩과 함께 꽁꽁 싸여 있다.

items.title: 콘서트·영화관·카페가 붐비는 이유? 수면族 때문!
items.snippet: 지난 10일 낮 12시 20분쯤 찾은 서울 강남구 ‘애니파크’. 만화책이나 보드게임 등을 즐기는 멀티카페지만, 이용객 20여 명이 점심시간을 이용해 각자 2평 안팎 방에서 낮잠을 자고 있었다. 카페 입구에는 담요와 쿠션 수십 개가 비치돼 있었다. 직장인 박모(43)씨는 “점심시간에 눈을 붙이고, 간단히 끼니도 해결할 수 있어서 1주일에 2~3번은 온다”고 했다. 카페 관계자는 “낮잠 수요가 많아 올해 초에는 1시간 이용권에 음식과 음료가 포함된 ‘직장인 세트’ 메뉴도 출시했다”고 말했다.

items.title: ‘남대문 스카프 아저씨’ 보조 알바 해보니… 아이돌급 환호에 이유 있었다
items.snippet: 그저 ‘남대문 스카프 아저씨(이하 아저씨)’와 몇 마디 나눠 볼 요량이었다. 평범한 시장 상인이 하루아침에 스타가 된 이유가 궁금했다. 그의 스카프 매장에서 일일 알바를 하게 될 줄은 몰랐다. 발단은 이렇다. 9일 오전 9시 50분쯤, 그가 일하는 서울 중구 남대문시장 ‘한양사’ 앞에는 손님 수십여 명이 줄을 서 있었다. 나도 그 틈에 끼어 있었다. 매장 오픈 전이었다.

items.title: 우리가 아는 다빈치의 얼굴, 누가 그렸을까
items.snippet: “그는 제게 훌륭한 아버지 같은 분이셨습니다. 제가 느끼는 슬픔은 이루 말할 수 없습니다. 살아 있는 한 저는 오래도록 이 슬픔을 안고 살아갈 것입니다.” 1519년 6월 1일, 프란체스코 멜치(Melzi)가 레오나르도 다빈치(da Vinci)의 형제들에게 보낸 편지의 한 대목이다. 스승을 잃은 제자는 비통한 상실감을 편지에 담았다. 한 달 전, 다빈치는 프랑스 앙부아즈의 클로 뤼세 저택에서 예순일곱 살로 생을 마감했다. 그는 죽음을 앞두고 공증인 앞에서 유언을 남겼다. 평생의 관찰과 연구가 담긴 노트와 드로잉, 회화 도구를 멜치에게 물려준다는 내용이었다. 당대 최고의 거장은 왜 혈육을 배제하고 젊은 제자에게 소중한 기록들을 맡겼을까. 멜치는 어떤 사람이었기에 다빈치의 절대적인 신뢰를 얻었을까.

items.title: 시키지도 않은 일까지 척척… 이 비서, 믿어도 될까
items.snippet: 최근 직장인 김모(44)씨는 스마트폰 화면을 보다가 가슴이 철렁 내려앉았다. 시키지도 않았는데 인공지능(AI) 비서가 직장 근처 식당 여러 곳에 전화를 건 것이다. 당황한 김씨가 이유를 묻자 “회식 장소를 추천해 달라고 하기에 예약이 가능한지 확인한 것”이라는 답이 돌아왔다. 질문에 답하는 데 그치지 않고 예약·결제 등 실제 업무까지 대신 처리하는 ‘AI 에이전트’가 국내에서도 확산하고 있다. 특히 한국어 맥락과 국내 생활 환경에 특화된 에이전트 서비스들이 출시되면서, 이른바 ‘IT 문외한’들도 손쉽게 AI 비서를 부리는 시대가 열렸다. 하지만 편리함만큼 우려도 작지 않다. 사람의 의도를 잘못 이해하거나, 지시하지 않은 일을 제멋대로 처리하는 일이 벌어지고 있기 때문이다.

items.title: 1500년 전 백제의 화려한 금빛 무늬
items.snippet: 예전에 국립공주박물관이 개최한 무령왕릉 발굴 50주년 기념 특별전을 보러 간 적이 있다. 전시 준비와 운영 업무로 담당 학예사는 피곤한 기색이 역력했지만, 어느 것 하나 허투루 볼 수 없는 알찬 유물들로 이루어진 전시를 보며 그를 부러워했던 기억이 있다. 유물에 귀천이 있는 것은 아니며, 미처 주목받지 못한 유물의 의미를 밝히는 것은 무척이나 보람된 일이다. 그러나 무령왕릉 출토품 수준의 유물을, 게다가 그 일괄을 가까이에서 보고 다루는 기회는 특별하다. 마치 김연아 선수의 최고 연기를 본 후에 다른 피겨스케이팅 선수의 실력을 한층 쉽게 가늠할 수 있는 것처럼, 이러한 경험 후에는 유물을 보는 안목과 시야가 달라지기 때문이다.

items.title: ‘내향인의 여행’부터 노벨상까지… 스톡홀름을 스쳐만 가선 안 된다
items.snippet: “패키지로 북유럽 여행을 오는 한국 여행객 대부분은 스웨덴에 하루밖에 시간을 내주지 않는다”고 스톡홀름 현지 가이드가 말했다. 실제 핀란드·스웨덴·노르웨이 3국을 방문한다는 북유럽 패키지도 일정을 뜯어보면 스웨덴에는 길어야 1박, 짧으면 반나절 잠시 머무르고 갈 뿐이다.

items.title: “켄차나~” “알았어데스!”를 대하는 우리의 자세
items.snippet: 외래어와 외국어의 홍수는 해가 바뀌고 계절이 바뀌어도 멈출 줄 모르는데 ‘외거어(外去語)’와 ‘한본어(韓本語)’ 소식이 가물에 콩 나는 것 이상으로 들려온다. 외거어는 우리말이 다른 언어에 들어가 쓰이는 말이고, 한본어는 우리말이 일본에 들어가 일본어와 섞여 쓰이고 있는 말이다. ‘오빠(oppa)’와 ‘언니(unni)’들이 해외에서 ‘대박(daebak)’을 낸 덕에 들려오는 소식이 고마우면서도 다른 한편으로는 말에 대한 이중적인 태도를 다시금 돌아보게 된다.

items.snippet: 미국에서 광복군을 후원한 호시한 지사(1885∼1956)와 러시아 연해주에서 독립운동을 하다 우즈베키스탄으로 강제 이주당한 이괄 지사(1898∼1963)의 유해가 고국으로 돌아온다. 우즈베키스탄에 안장된 독립유공자의 유해가 국내로 봉환되는 것은 이번이 처음이다.국가보훈부는 제87회 순국선열의 날(17일)을 앞두고 두 지사와 배우자들의 유해를 15일 인천국제공항을 통해 봉환한다고 13일 밝혔다. 권오을 보훈부 장관이 공항에서 유해를 직접 영접할 계획이다. 유해 봉환식은 16일 서울 서대문독립공원 3·1독립선언기념탑에서 열린다. 보훈부는 호 지사가 서대문형무소에 수감됐던 이력을 고려했다고 설명했다. 두 지사의 유해는 이후 국립대전현충원에 안장된다.서울 교남동 출신인 호 지사는 1914년 미국에서 한인소년병학교 운영을 지원하는 단체를 조직했고, 3...

items.title: AnalogLayoutWorld: An Open Benchmark for Agentic Analog Layout Design
items.abstract: Coding agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in software development, yet their ability to tackle long-horizon engineering tasks governed by physical constraints remains less understood. We study this question through analog circuit layout, which demands domain knowledge, geometric reasoning, and iterative interaction with design and verification tools. We introduce \textbf{AnalogLayoutWorld}, an open-source agent benchmark with 40 expert-reviewed tasks for end-to-end layout generation from fixed transistor-level netlists. It combines an integrated design environment with independent physical and post-layout electrical verification, as well as objective layout quality metrics co-designed with analog layout experts. items.title: Interfacial Effects of Thermal Reorganization on Charge and Spin Transport in Organic Spin Valves
items.abstract: Organic semiconductors are attractive for spintronic applications owing to their weak spin-orbit coupling, small hyperfine interactions, mechanical flexibility, and tunable electronic properties. Organic spin valves (OSVs) provide a representative platform for investigating spin-dependent transport. However, the magnetoresistance (MR) response is highly sensitive to the ferromagnetic electrode/organic semiconductor interface (spinterface). Variations in interfacial morphology, chemical interaction, energy-level alignment, and spin polarization can strongly affect spin injection, transport, and detection, making reproducible OSV performance difficult to achieve. Here, we investigate how in situ thermal annealing affects the electrical and magnetotransport properties of complete NDI-based OSVs. items.title: Gatemon qubits based on in-situ ternary InAsSb/Al nanowire Josephson junctions
items.abstract: Ternary InAsSb/Al nanowires combine compositionally engineerable semiconductor properties with epitaxial proximity superconductivity, making them attractive for hybrid quantum circuits and mesoscopic superconductivity. Here, we realize gatemon qubits based on shadow-defined in-situ InAsSb/Al Josephson junctions in a single growth process. Gate-dependent microwave spectroscopy demonstrates electrostatic tuning of the qubit transition over several gigahertz. Rabi oscillations and Ramsey interference show coherent qubit control, with representative values T1 = 0.79 us and T2* = 0.91 us. Across five gatemons distributed over three chips, the measured relaxation times range from approximately 0.2 us to 1 us and decrease with increasing qubit frequency. items.title: Progress on the MALTA CMOS Sensor: Edge-TCT Measurements for Parametric Pixel Simulation
items.abstract: MALTA2 is a monolithic active pixel sensor, developed in the 180 nm CMOS imaging technology for radiation-hard applications in high-rate environments. This contribution summarizes recent developments in the characterization and simulation of MALTA2. The charge collection of a sensor on epitaxial silicon is studied with the Edge Transient Current Technique (Edge-TCT), using a digital readout, where the charge is reconstructed solely from binary hit data. In previous works, only specially designed analog output pixels at the matrix periphery were investigated. In contrast, the digital readout gives access to the full edge of the pixel matrix. Laser scans across neighboring pixels enable a two-dimensional parameterization of the charge collection. items.title: Bright and Uniform Silicon Carbide Nanophotonic Arrays for Scalable Nanoscale Quantum Sensing
items.abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) spin defects are emerging as powerful platforms for nanoscale quantum sensing due to their near-surface stability, near-infrared emission, and CMOS compatibility. However, poor photon collection efficiency and the reliance on randomly distributed defects hinder the realization of practical, large-scale devices. Here, we demonstrate scalable, ultra-bright, and highly uniform SiC quantum nanophotonic arrays. By combining a self-aligned fabrication process with localized oxygen ion implantation, we deterministically position PL5 and PL6 centers at the exact center of 4H-SiC nanopillars. This architecture yields record-high photon count rates of $\sim$1 Mcps (PL5) and $\sim$2 Mcps (PL6), establishing a new benchmark for SiC color centers while maintaining near-identical brightness across the array. items.title: High-Quality InSb Nanowires Grown by Molecular-Beam Epitaxy via Precise Catalyst Modulation
items.abstract: Semiconductor InSb nanowires are a major material candidate for topological quantum computation. The nanowires in current devices were mostly grown using metal organic chemical vapor deposition, incompatible with in situ growth of superconductor, a crucial requirement for low-disorder devices. Growth of InSb nanowires using molecular-beam epitaxy (MBE) can address this issue. So far, studies on MBE-grown InSb remain limited due to an extremely narrow parameter window for the growth and reproducibility. Moreover, the use of foreign catalysts can introduce deep-level impurities. Here, we report a self-catalyzed MBE growth of InSb nanowires without those foreign catalysts. We first grow GaAs nanowire stems, and then convert Ga catalyst droplets into In droplets in situ. Axial heteroepitaxial growth of InSb can be realized through the In droplets on top of GaAs stems. items.title: Self-Supervised Attention-Based Virtual Metrology for CMP MRR Prediction
items.abstract: Chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) is a critical semiconductor manufacturing process where material removal rate (MRR) is a key metric for process monitoring and advanced process control (APC). Virtual metrology enables MRR estimation from process time series signals, supporting run-to-run(R2R) control and process optimization while reducing reliance on physical metrology. Existing approaches typically rely on simplified linear assumptions or require handcrafted feature engineering. In this paper, we propose Global Regression Pretraining(GREP), a self-supervised, attention-based framework for CMP MRR prediction. GREP learns temporal representations from unlabeled sensor signals through global proxy-target regression, followed by supervised fine-tuning for MRR estimation. items.title: Integrated optical isolators enabled by 2D semiconductors via spin-momentum locking
items.abstract: Integrated optical isolators based on spin-momentum locking hold great potential for protecting photonic integrated circuits from unwanted reflections. Currently, the most common implementations are magneto-optical isolators that require an externally applied magnetic field. Nevertheless, a wide range of nonreciprocal effects remains to be exploited in alternative material platforms. Although the majority of these effects induce changes to the propagation of light as a function of its polarization, they can be directly connected to the propagation direction through spin-momentum locking. We employ a computational approach to investigate various designs of integrated isolators based on nonreciprocal 2D semiconductors, studying the influence of their geometry and optical properties on the device performance. items.title: Quantum geometric bounds and uncertainty relations for velocity variance and spread of Wannier function
items.abstract: By utilizing the derivation of quantum Cramér-Rao bound and an argument put forward by Efimov and Dodonov, we derive several uncertainty relations for mixed states that constrain the diagonal product, trace, and each diagonal element of the covariance matrix of multiple observables. By choosing the observables to be the symmetric logarithmic derivative, the uncertainty relations imply various geometric bounds on quantum Fisher information matrix caused by mean Uhlmann curvature, which in pure states become geometric bounds on quantum metric caused by Berry curvature. Our formalism reveals optical sum rules for velocity variance and spread of valence band Wannier functions, and how they are bounded by the Berry curvature and commutator of velocity operators. items.title: Development and characterization of monolithic sensors with internal gain in a 110 nm CMOS process
items.abstract: This paper presents the optimization and characterization of a Monolithic Active Pixel Sensor with internal gain implemented in the 110 nm CMOS process from LFoundry. This work, carried out within the framework of the latest ARCADIA production run, reports on the characterization of sensors with an optimized gain layer. Improvements over earlier prototypes, including substrate current reduction via guard-ring connection, are briefly discussed. Both laboratory and in-beam measurements are presented. Using soft X-rays from a 55Fe source, both the pixel response and the noise performance are analyzed. In addition, laser measurements demonstrate an electronic jitter ranging from 20 to 40 ps for a signal amplitude corresponding to one minimum ionizing particle (MIP). items.title: Cation-intermixing driven evolution from a narrow avoided crossing to an enlarged inverted gap in Ge$_2$Bi$_2$Te$_5$
items.abstract: Combining the building blocks and structural motifs of the topological insulator Bi$_2$Te$_3$ and the ferroelectric Rashba semiconductor GeTe, we synthesized and comprehensively characterized the resulting Ge$_2$Bi$_2$Te$_5$ compound, which exhibits pronounced cation intermixing. Using momentum-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and ab initio calculations, we demonstrate how cation intermixing drives the evolution of its electronic structure from a narrow avoided crossing to a substantially enlarged inverted band gap. items.title: Large-scale characterisation of silicon T centres with tuning-free broadband cavities
items.abstract: T centres in silicon combine an optical transition in the telecom O-band with a long-lived electron and nuclear spin in a photonics- and CMOS-compatible host. However, weak emission of photons in the zero-phonon line (ZPL) makes measurements slow. Cavities can increase the ZPL photon emission, but high-Q cavities require individual tuning to the T centre wavelength, hindering statistical understanding of T centre properties. Here, we overcome this limitation by developing low-Q confocally-addressable cavities. We create an array of 400 cavities, detuned $0.0\pm 1.1$ nm from the T centre, with an average quality factor of $298\pm 78$. The combination of high accuracy and moderate quality factors removes the need for individual tuning. The array yields a median T centre signal increase of $6.5\times$, corresponding to a $42\times$ measurement speedup. Studying the cavity statistics enables...

items.title: Nitride crystalline barrier epitaxial SIS Josephson junctions by MBE
items.abstract: Superconductor-insulator-superconductor Josephson junctions with crystalline tunnel barriers have remained elusive by epitaxial techniques such as MOCVD or MBE that produce the junction materials and devices powering today's electronic and photonic systems like transistors and lasers. Here, we overcome the key materials hurdle to realize the first functional nitride crystalline barrier Josephson junctions by MBE. Despite an AlN barrier thickness of approximately 4.5 nm, the NbN/AlN/NbN trilayers exhibit coherent Josephson tunneling with critical current densities of approximately 17 A/cm2, an IcRn product of approximately 2.5 mV, and a superconducting gap voltage of approximately 3.7 mV with a BCS-like gap evolution with temperature. items.abstract: State-of-the-art atomistic foundation models provide broadly transferable energy and force predictions, but their direct deployment in large-scale molecular dynamics remains computationally costly. Here we examine whether their knowledge can be distilled into compact potentials while retaining the physical responses of heterogeneous semiconductor interfaces. items.title: Correlation-Consistent Gaussian Basis Sets for Periodic Solids. I. Hydrogen and p-block Elements from Boron to Chlorine
items.abstract: We present the cc-pVXZ-s series (X = D, T, and Q) of correlation-consistent Gaussian basis sets for solids, covering hydrogen and the p-block elements from boron to chlorine. The series includes basis sets of consistent quality for the all-electron potential and for various pseudopotentials and effective core potentials commonly used in periodic calculations. Our design combines Dunning's construction of the molecular cc-pVXZ series with a revised material-constrained atomic optimization (MCAO) algorithm for improved numerical performance. MCAO regularizes standard atomic optimization to suppress overly diffuse basis functions and ensure numerical stability in a set of reference solids. items.title: Squeezed Light Generation by Cooper Pair Recombination in a Superconductor-Semiconductor Structure
items.abstract: We theoretically demonstrate squeezed light generation in a compact, electrically driven device utilizing the nonlinear light-matter interaction of Cooper-pair recombination in a hybrid superconductorsemiconductor structure. On the basis of second-order perturbation theory, we developed an effective Hamiltonian which incorporates the electronic component of the interaction as a photon coupling strength coefficient, enabling a model to describe the quadrature squeezing effect of Cooper-pair recombination on the photonic state. We find the squeezing strength to be proportional to the superconducting energy gap squared and device length, as well as increasing with applied voltage. For practical device length, materials and voltage bias, we calculated squeezing values comparable to those of existing squeezed light generation methods when operating below the critical temperature. items.title: Quantum Thermal Transistor via Nonlinear Environmental Coupling
items.abstract: Thermal amplification enables sensitive control of heat currents, providing a basis for heat management and thermal signal processing in quantum devices. For a harmonic oscillator coupled to emitter, collector, and base thermal reservoirs, we recover the absence of thermal amplification when system-reservoir interactions permit only single-quantum exchange. A controlled weak-nonlinearity expansion, supported by numerical stationary solutions, shows that two-quantum exchange at the emitter enables amplification and predicts its onset. When two-quantum exchange dominates at the emitter and collector, varying the base temperature redistributes populations between even and odd oscillator sectors. This changes the emitter and collector heat currents far more than the base current, enabling large thermal amplification. items.title: Analysis and Demonstration of a Current-Stiff, Isolated Capacitive Bridge Transformer
items.abstract: The traditional Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) based Dual Active Bridge (DAB) utilizes a transformer at its center to provide galvanic isolation and a turns ratio for step up/down functionality. However, the transformer is often the limiting factor of the DAB, especially as semiconductor switching speeds improve, given steel core losses, winding losses, etc. This paper presents a new DAB architecture based on Current Source Inverters (CSIs) coupled through, and isolated by, an AC capacitive bridge, yielding a system called a Capacitive Bridge Transformer (CBT). The CBT architecture eliminates all magnetic components in the AC portion of the isolated DAB circuit, reducing frequency scaling barriers normally present in DABs. Electrical Stark Tuning and In Situ Field Sensing of $V_{2}$ Silicon Vacancies in a 4H-SiC a-Plane Lateral pin-Diode
items.abstract: Silicon carbide has emerged as a highly promising platform for scalable quantum technologies, with the silicon vacancy serving as a robust spin qubit and quantum sensor. However, conventional c-plane 4H-SiC restricts the experimental scheme and resonant optical excitation to the sample's geometry. The usage of a-plane substrates enables more versatile resonant optical access to the color center through the wafer surface. Here, we demonstrate the electrical control and optical addressability of $V_{2}$ (cubic lattice site) silicon vacancies within the intrinsic region of lateral pin-diodes fabricated on a-plane 4H-SiC wafers using a scalable complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) process. Despite extensive semiconductor processing, the integrated color centers exhibit good optical quality, evidenced by narrow optical transition linewidths below 80 MHz at zero bias. These embedded...

items.title: Nanostructuring Semiconductor Surfaces Using Self-Assembled Metal Nanoparticles for Optoelectronic Applications
items.abstract: Semiconductor nanostructures are key light-management elements because their geometry can strengthen light-matter interaction, suppress reflection, and enhance optical coupling. Yet their adoption across material platforms is constrained by lithography, multistep pattern transfer, persistent masks, and material-specific etching. Here, we introduce a lithography-free two-step strategy in which thermally evaporated self-assembled Ga nanoparticles act as self-consuming masks during Ar inductively coupled plasma reactive-ion etching. Correlated transmission electron microscopy on GaAs reveals the formation mechanism. Comparable erosion of the Ga nanoparticles and exposed substrate progressively converts Ga-capped pedestals into pure semiconductor nanocones while preserving crystalline order. items.title: From Growth to Devices: Oxygen-Controlled Superconductivity in BSCCO Thin Films
items.abstract: Realizing device-compatible high-$T_c$ superconductors requires simultaneous control of oxygen stoichiometry and tolerance to nanofabrication. Here, we investigate sputtered Bi$_2$Sr$_2$Ca$_{n-1}$Cu$_n$O$_{2n+4+δ}$ (BSCCO) thin films and establish a direct link between annealing conditions, oxygen incorporation, and superconducting transport. By independently varying the annealing temperature and duration, we identify an optimal annealing condition of $860\,^{\circ}$C for 3\,h, which yields the highest superconducting transition temperature and the narrowest transition among the investigated samples. X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy, and X-ray photoemission spectroscopy reveal a non-monotonic evolution of lattice oxygen, which governs hole doping in the CuO$_2$ planes and produces the characteristic dome-like dependence of $T_c$ on doping concentration. items.title: SLIC: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning Small LMs for Multi-Turn Analog Circuit Optimization
items.abstract: Analog integrated circuit (IC) design is a multi-turn, simulator-grounded engineering task that demands iterative reasoning over coupled performance tradeoffs, yet proprietary process design kits (PDKs) make hosted large language model workflows difficult to deploy in practical design settings. We present SLIC (Small LM Iterating on Circuits), a reinforcement fine-tuning framework that trains a 4B-scale, locally deployable language model for closed-loop analog circuit optimization. SLIC pairs structured circuit representations with discretized relative-update actions, domain- and success-gated multiobjective rewards, and Reward-Guided Rollout Steering (RGRS), which turns per-step simulator feedback into signals for both policy learning and online rollout construction in this sparse, highly constrained domain. items.title: 5G CATS: 5G-Based Cryptographic Authorization Against Trafficking of Semiconductor Devices
items.abstract: Enforcing export controls on AI accelerators requires verifying where a chip operates after deployment. Round-trip time measurements can bound a chip's distance from a trusted landmark, but any jitter in honest replies forces the verifier to loosen its timeout, giving an attacker slack to relay traffic over fiber from a restricted region. Prior approaches either cross the untrusted host stack or rely on noisy power-line channels that inflate this slack. We present 5G CATS, a location certification system that pairs a co-packaged 5G radio, cryptographic engine, and hardware interlock on the GPU package with 5G Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) base stations. Terminating the radio link inside the package removes the host software, PCIe fabric, and baseboard management controller from the verification path. items.title: Ultrafast Hole Transport and Electron Localization in Superatomic Re$_{6}$Se$_{8}$Cl$_{2}$
items.abstract: Van der Waals superatomic crystals represent an intriguing class of materials, exhibiting unique ultrafast electronic and structural responses arising from their hierarchical crystal structure. These materials bridge the properties of semiconductors, molecular solids, and nanocrystal arrays, hosting a range of many-body interactions that can be controlled with atomically precise structures. To establish the structure-function correlation, it is necessary to understand element-specific electronic states arising from complex superatomic unit cells. Here, we use transient XUV spectroscopy to individually probe the dynamics of photoexcited electrons and holes in Re$_{6}$Se$_{8}$Cl$_{2}$ superatomic crystals. items.abstract: Physical synapses are routinely described by a single number, the weight, that is identified with a conductance, a current, or a luminescence yield. This identification conflates two different objects: the internal state that the device stores, and the signal obtained when that state is read. Building on Chua's formulation of memristive systems, we separate the state variable, which evolves with the excitation history, from the observation map that converts it into a measured signal, and we define the weight as the outcome of a specified read protocol. items.abstract: We study the spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet with an anisotropic $Γ$ term on a zigzag ladder, which can be exactly mapped to the spin-1/2 XYZ zigzag ladder by a spin rotation. This model has recently attracted considerable interest as an effective model for the quasi-one-dimensional magnetic semiconductor YbCuS$_2$. For the model, the ground-state phase diagram was previously proposed by Saito and Hotta [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 166701 (2024); Phys. Rev. B 110, 024409 (2024)]. We systematically reexamine the phase diagram through complementary numerical and analytical approaches, including exact diagonalization, the density-matrix renormalization group method, and low-energy effective theories. items.title: Neutronic Field-Effect Transistor
items.abstract: Field-effect electronic devices are in widespread use in communication, computing, data storage, and sensing applications. We demonstrate a neutronic field-effect transistor (NFET) that is analogous to the Datta-Das electron spin transistor and atomtronic devices. The NFET is based on a perfect-crystal Mach-Zehnder neutron interferometer with phase shifts applied to the spin and path degrees of freedom.

items.title: Spin-valve effect through electrostatic coupling
items.abstract: We propose a spin-valve effect in which an insulating magnetic van der Waals multilayer controls the conductance of an adjacent non-magnetic conductor by electrostatic coupling, without transport-electrons entering the magnetic layers. The coupling is induced by the variations of the electronic structure when the relative orientation of the magnetization of adjacent monolayers changes from parallel to antiparallel, modifying both the dielectric constant and band alignment. We consider two types of coupling and device concepts: charge transfer to a graphene monolayer and capacitive coupling in a single-electron transistor. We use density functional calculations to assess the magnitude of the effect in various materials, including CrI$_3$, CrBr$_3$, CrCl$_3$ and NiBr$_2$. items.title: Gate-tunable supercurrent switching in a three-terminal quantum dot transistor
items.abstract: We propose and analyze a three-terminal superconducting transistor switch in which a gate-defined quantum dot region interrupts a flux-controlled loop. The output supercurrent is switched off completely when the two loop arms couple to the dot with equal tunneling strengths and half a flux quantum threads the loop. The device then operates as a symmetric SQUID at half flux. The condition follows from a single geometric factor $χ$, which reduces the three-terminal problem to an equivalent two-terminal Anderson impurity model and makes the switching mechanism independent of the Coulomb interaction, the dot level position, the total hybridization and temperature. These enter only through a prefactor and thus decide how tolerant the device is to imperfect barrier tuning. items.title: Impact of multi-dot configurations on electron temperature and double quantum dot latching in gate-controlled qubit devices
items.abstract: Many currently envisaged scalable architectures for Si/SiGe spin qubit devices utilize gate-controlled multi-dot configurations characterized by their peculiar Coulomb blockade physics. One example is the concurrent use of a single electron transistor (SET) as a charge sensor and as a reservoir for adjacent qubit quantum dots (QD). We find that the SET energy spectrum impacts pulsed gate spectroscopy of the QD when the SET simultaneously acts as the reservoir and the sensor. Then, using the qubit QD as a probe, we quantify how strongly the electron temperature of the SET depends on the applied bias. It surpasses a reference experiment by 100 $mK$ even at 50 $μV$ bias. items.abstract: Three-phase ac-ac converters for variable-speed drives can be realized conventionally as voltage-source converters (VSCs) or, leveraging emerging monolithic bidirectional GaN power transistors (M-BDSs), as current-source converters (CSCs). This paper presents a comparative life-cycle assessment of a realized VSC and a CSC demonstrators including grid-side and motor-side EMI filters, and with identical specifications (1.4 kW rated power, 200 V line-to-line rms grid and motor voltage). items.title: Rapid Heat Removal from Chip Cores: Near-Junction Active Cooling of Power Transistors via Electron Entropy Transport and Spatial Decoupling
items.abstract: Chip performance is limited by a shared bottleneck: the core produces heat faster than it can be moved out. We study the hardest case, RF power GaN HEMTs, whose hotspots exceed 5 kW/cm^2, and propose a horizontal near-junction active cooling topology built on electron entropy transport. Classical on-chip thermoelectric cooling faces a contest: Peltier absorption grows linearly with current, Joule heating with its square. In a vertical pillar, its own conduction resistance locks about half the Joule heat back toward the cold end, capping net cooling. From the Onsager framework we show the origin of this asymmetry: Peltier absorption localizes at the interface where the Seebeck coefficient jumps, whereas Joule heating fills the volume. items.title: Orbital texture of valence band and interband transitions of the type-II multiferroic van der Waals NiI$_2$
items.abstract: NiI$_2$ is a van der Waals semiconductor characterized by complex electronic and magnetic phases, holding promise towards functional applications. For this purpose, a detailed understanding of its band structure and its excitations is essential to elucidate the electronic and transport properties. We present a comprehensive description of the band structure and of the lowest valence-to-conduction band transition in bulk NiI$_2$, by means of time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy supported by first-principles calculations. We describe the orbital character of Ni and I manifolds, and identify the main momentum-resolved features of the valence band and the shallow minima of the conduction band. With this study, we provide a foundational understanding of the electronic structure of NiI$_2$ and its single-particle interband electronic excitation, a benchmark for theoretical model...

items.title: A Per-Step Load-Balancing Engine for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving
items.abstract: In expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts serving, a layer finishes only when the most loaded GPU of its group does. Token routing shifts at every decode step and concentrates on a few experts, so most of the group's reserved GPU time waits on stragglers. Recovering that time means re-deciding, at every layer of every decode step, how each replicated expert's tokens divide between its copies. The exact linear-program solvers that make this decision optimally take longer than many of the layers they serve, and their working set outgrows GPU shared memory at deployment scale. We introduce Relief, a bidirectional pairwise relaxation that makes the linear program unnecessary, coming within a fraction of a point of the per-step optimum in a few passes of integer halving over the token counts. We build and measure three deployments, CUDA kernels on the serving GPU, the same verified engine on an F...

items.title: ICLayout-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Custom Circuit Layout Design
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are being explored for circuit design, but their ability to produce high-quality custom layouts has not been extensively evaluated. ICLayout-Bench is a benchmark in which agents use electronic design automation (EDA) tools to construct and optimize GDSII layouts from transistor-level circuit netlists. These layouts are evaluated using physical verification, parasitic extraction, and post-layout simulation. Layouts that pass the physical and functional checks are scored on electrical performance and area. The benchmark includes 165 tasks across 13 process design kits (PDKs), covering technology nodes from 3 nm to 180 nm. The tasks span analog, mixed-signal, and digital circuits in open-source and commercial EDA flows. The experiments evaluate 22 configurations spanning seven models on 21 public and 19 private tasks. Mean layout scores range from 4.22 to 8...

items.title: $>3\text{ W/mm}$ Output Power $\mathrm{Al}_{0.61}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.39}\mathrm{N}$ Channel HEMT with $24.4\%$ Associated PAE at $10\text{ GHz}$
items.abstract: In this work, an ultra-wide bandgap (UWBG) high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) was fabricated using an $\mathrm{Al}_{0.76}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.24}\mathrm{N}$ barrier and an $\mathrm{Al}_{0.61}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.39}\mathrm{N}$ channel with thick $\mathrm{SiO}_2$ passivation. The device demonstrated low current collapse at $40\text{ V}$ drain bias. At $10\text{ GHz}$, the device exhibited an output power of $3.07\text{ W/mm}$ with an associated power-added efficiency (PAE) of $24.4\%$. A peak PAE of $33.9\%$ was achieved at an associated output power of $2.14\text{ W/mm}$. This excellent large-signal performance highlights the strong potential of UWBG $\mathrm{AlGaN}$ channel devices for X-band applications.

items.title: Demonstration of High fmax (> 80 GHz) in Recessed-Gate and Passivated $\mathrm{Al_{0.60}Ga_{0.40}N}$ Channel RF HEMTs
items.abstract: In this work, ultra-wide bandgap (UWBG) $\mathrm{Al_{0.60}Ga_{0.40}N}$ channel high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) with an $\mathrm{Al_{0.81}Ga_{0.19}N}$ barrier and an $\mathrm{Al_{0.86}Ga_{0.14}N}$ back barrier were fabricated. The devices featured a recessed T-gate structure and $\mathrm{SiO_2}$ passivation. Scaled devices achieved a cutoff frequency ($f_{\mathrm{T}}$) of 35 GHz, a maximum oscillation frequency ($f_{\mathrm{max}}$) of 82 GHz, and an average breakdown field $> 3 \mathrm{MV/cm}$, while maintaining a reasonable current collapse of $\sim 20\%$ under a 40 V drain bias in pinch-off condition. Devices with larger dimensions demonstrated a high off-state breakdown voltage of 883 V and an $f_{\mathrm{T}}$ of 24 GHz, yielding a high Johnson's figure of merit ($\mathrm{JFOM}$) of 21.19 $\mathrm{THz \cdot V}$. items.title: Deterministically fabricated C-band single-photon sources based on quantum dot circular Bragg grating cavities
items.abstract: Telecom-wavelength quantum light sources are essential components for scalable fiber-based quantum networks, where on-demand emission of single photons is required for high secret key rates. Here, we demonstrate the deterministic integration of metal-organic vapor-phase epitaxy (MOVPE)-grown C-band InAs/InP quantum dots into circular Bragg grating resonators. The integrated emitters exhibit a radiative lifetime of $T_1 = (1400 \pm 50)~\mathrm{ps}$ and a spectral linewidth of $ΔE_{\mathrm{FWHM}} = (41.0 \pm 4.0)~μ\mathrm{eV}$. Under non-resonant excitation, we measure a post-selected single-photon purity of $(0.95 \pm 0.02)$ and a raw two-photon interference visibility of $V_{12\mathrm{ns}} = (35 \pm 2)\%$, which increases to $(70 \pm 18)\%$ under temporal post-selection. We discuss strategies to improve photon indistinguishability, including radiative-rate engineering, charge stabilizati...

items.title: Wafer-scale MoS2 and HZO-based Ferroelectric Field Effect Transistors with 4.4 V Memory Window for Back-End Compatible Multibit Memory
items.abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) with low-power operation and non-volatile data retention enabled by stable ferroelectric polarization switching, have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional floating-gate transistors for next-generation low-power memory applications. A FeFET with two-dimensional (2D) channel provides the opportunity for better electrostatic gate control and scalability beyond silicon. In this work, we report wafer scale 2D semiconductor-based FeFETs with Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) gate stack showing unusual p-type charge transport and stable multibit memory properties. FeFETs based on 2-3 monolayer Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) channel and a 20 nm HZO back gate oxide layer exhibit a large hysteresis with a memory window spanning 4.4 V under a operating voltage range of +3.8 to -3.8 V, and an ION/IOFF ratio of 10^5. We demonstrate that the polarization char...

items.title: Hands-on fabrication of 2D material field-effect transistors for the classroom using off-the-shelf ionic gel
items.abstract: We introduce a hands-on experimental method that enables students to fabricate and operate van der Waals semiconductor-based field-effect transistors (FETs) using readily available materials and minimal infrastructure. The approach is based on ionic-gel gating using commercially available hydrogel conductors originally developed for muscle electrostimulation devices. For device fabrication we rely on commercially available thin-film interdigitated electrode arrays and for the semiconductor channel, we deposited MoS2 flakes produced by high-throughput mechanical exfoliation. By avoiding the need for cleanroom processing, vacuum deposition, or custom electrolytes, this method allows functional FETs based on van der Waals materials to be realized in a standard teaching laboratory. The experiment is well suited for undergraduate and early graduate courses and is intended to complement concep...

items.title: Dopant Cluster Engineering for Tunable Room-Temperature Ferromagnetism in 2D Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
items.abstract: Two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides (2D-TMDs) offer a promising platform for realizing dilute magnetic semiconductors. However, simultaneously achieving large magnetic anisotropy energy (MAE) and high Curie temperature (T$_\text{c}$) remains a major challenge. In this work, we employ DFT+U to systematically investigate the thermodynamic stability and magnetic properties of 2D-MoSe$_2$ and 2D-WSe$_2$ doped with transition metal atoms. We found that the paired dopant configurations are more stable than previously attributed isolated dopants. Despite their nearly identical crystal structures, 2D-MoSe$_2$ and 2D-WSe$_2$ show contrasting properties upon doping. All paired dopants in 2D-MoSe$_2$ exhibit long-range ferromagnetic coupling (FMC) primarily due to carrier-mediated exchange interactions, whereas those in 2D-WSe$_2$ show weak exchange coupling. items.title: Fabrication and Characterization of Flexible In2O3 Thin-Film Transistors on Mica Substrates
items.abstract: Flexible oxide-semiconductor thin-film transistors (TFTs) with high field-effect mobility (uFE > 70 cm^2/Vs) are required for next-generation flexible displays. Polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs are promising candidates; however, conventional flexible substrates such as plastics are not suitable because their fabrication typically requires relatively high temperatures (~350 deg.C). In this study, we used mica as a flexible substrate to fabricate polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs, motivated by previous demonstrations of crystalline oxide growth on mica. The resulting TFTs exhibited a uFE of approximately 75 cm^2/Vs. The devices maintained gate-modulated operation after 10^3 flex-out bending cycles at a 5 mm radius, whereas flex-in cycling caused early electrical failure, likely due to In2O3 film degradation. The TFTs also operated normally after exposure to 85 deg.C and 40% relative humidit...

items.title: The World Model Planning Accelerator (WMPA): Hardware-Algorithm Co-Design for Embedded AI in Robotics
items.abstract: Embedded AI is moving from perception to prediction. Robots now use world models$\unicode{x2014}$learned simulators that predict the outcome of candidate actions in a compressed latent space before any is executed. Every predicted step must be computed on board within a tight power and thermal budget, yet the energy these steps fundamentally require, and how far real hardware sits from it, have not been characterized. We derive lower bounds on the arithmetic operations and the CMOS dynamic energy of a latent state transition from information theory and Boolean circuit complexity. Profiling a DreamerV3-style Recurrent State Space Model (RSSM) shows that every rollout operation is memory-bandwidth bound and that a GPU consumes at least $5.9\times10^{10}$ times the CMOS energy floor. items.title: How light interacts with matter, revisited
items.abstract: In 1968 Victor Weisskopf explained in Scientific American how light interacts with matter, with a few formulas and many words. We tell the same story again with the tools that have since become available: the fields are computed and drawn, and their evolution in time is shown in animations. Light is described as a classical electromagnetic field and matter as a collection of charged oscillators; every phenomenon follows from adding up the retarded waves radiated by the oscillators, each with its proper delay and phase. From this single picture we obtain the blue of the sky and the white of the clouds, transparency and the refractive index, the Ewald-Oseen extinction theorem, reflection and the colours of thin films, why metals reflect and what gives metals and semiconductors their colours, polarizers, Brewster's angle and birefringence, the working of mirrors, lenses, microscopes and the...

items.title: Controlled Oxidation of Tellurium Nanoparticles for Telecom Detection
items.abstract: Surface oxidation plays an important role in governing charge transport in semiconductor nanoparticle assemblies. Here, we investigate the optoelectronic properties of solution-processed tellurium (Te) nanoparticle ensembles prepared through gradual ambient-air exposure. Structural and spectroscopic analyses reveal interconnected elemental Te nanoparticles with coexisting alpha-TeO2 and hydroxyl-containing surface species, exhibiting a lower relative contribution of oxidized Te than previously investigated forced-air-oxidized ensembles. The resulting photodetectors demonstrate photoresponse at 405, 532, and 1550 nm, with maximum responsivities of 10.1, 14.4, and 8.5 mA/W, respectively. At 1550 nm, the device exhibits rise and fall times of 17.7 and 40.2 s, respectively, and an estimated shot-noise-limited specific detectivity of 1.3 * 10^6 Jones. items.title: Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits
items.abstract: Logical qubits encoded in collective states of multiple spins are promising building blocks for large-scale semiconductor quantum processors. As novel fault-tolerant architectures increasingly rely on qubit shuttling, understanding decoherence of the shuttled multi-spin qubits becomes crucial. We analyze fidelity and leakage of the logical qubits dephased by the spatio-temporally correlated $1/f$ noise, considering two-, three-, and four-spin encodings. We study different shuttling protocols and establish that for all encodings generally, parallel shuttling provides the best protection against decoherence at short distances, whereas sequential shuttling outperforms others for long-range transport (although the exact boundaries depend on the specific device parameters). We explain this common behavior in terms of the dephasing factors of pairs of the shuttled spins; we provide explicit ex...

items.title: Discrete time crystals and heteroclinic switching in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers
items.abstract: We investigate the mechanisms underlying the emergence of discrete time crystals in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers. Our analysis is based on a Haus master equation generalized to retain carrier memory between round-trips. We perform a detailed bifurcation analysis that reveals a well-defined hierarchy of subharmonic states, illustrating how pulses may suppress their neighbors when the modulation runs faster than the pulse round-trip frequency. To identify the underlying mechanism, we derive effective equations of motion that couple the pulse energies, their positions relative to the modulation transmission maxima, and the local time-dependent gain. These reveal that transitions between time-crystalline states occur via transcritical global bifurcations, opening a regime of heteroclinic winnerless competition between symmetry-degenerate configurations.

items.title: Microscopic theory of exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides
items.abstract: Polarons are composite quasiparticles formed when charge carriers strongly couple to lattice vibrations, manifesting as carriers dressed by a surrounding cloud of phonons. Although this dressing fundamentally renormalizes the effective mass and mobility of carriers, its impact on electrically neutral exciton polarons in 2D semiconductors has received limited attention. In particular, despite the growing interest in polaronic effects in atomically thin semiconductors, only a few theoretical studies have addressed spectral signatures and renormalized properties of exciton polarons in these materials. Here, we develop a microscopic model to describe exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides. Applying this model to $1s$ acoustic polarons in an MoSe$_2$ monolayer, we reveal a distinct kink in the polaron dispersion, accompanied by a pronounced broadening of its spectral function. T...

items.title: Exciton design via topological spin textures
items.abstract: Excitons carry energy and information through a semiconductor without carrying charge. This makes them attractive for optoelectronics, but also hard to guide. Magnetic skyrmions, on the other hand, are moved by small electrical currents. Here we develop a theory of excitons interacting with a skyrmion in which the electron and the hole are treated as distinct constituents, each with its own spin--orbit coupling. We find that the topology of the skyrmion is transferred to the exciton only when the exchange coupling exceeds the relevant spin--orbit splitting. The exciton then experiences a full flux quantum, with opposite signs in the two valleys. The quantum metric of the spin texture creates a ring-shaped barrier that traps excitons, whereas the topological charge fixes the angular momentum of the trapped states and hence their optical selection rules. items.title: Advances in High-Precision Astrometry for Exoplanet Detection for Astrometric Missions
items.abstract: High-precision astrometry is a cornerstone for detecting Earth-like exoplanets in the habitable zones of nearby solar-type stars and probing the nature of dark matter in galactic environments. Achieving sub-microarcsecond accuracy requires unprecedented control over detector morphology, optical distortion, and astrometric measurement techniques. This paper reviews recent progress in characterizing large format detector at the micropixel scale level, calibrating optical distortion using reference stars, and refining differential astrometry methods to detect the faint astrometric signatures of Earth-mass exoplanets. We highlight the latest developments in the RETINA project, which aims to advance the TRL of GIGAPYX 220 MP CMOS detectors from Pyxalis which are critical components for future space missions such as ESA's Theia and NASA's Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). The project focuses...

items.title: On the collective flow puzzle in ultra-central heavy-ion collisions
items.abstract: Using UCC-DiffHIC, an AI-accelerated event-by-event hydrodynamic model validated against hybrid simula- tions, we study flow in ultracentral Pb-Pb collisions. For suitable initial conditions, the calculated v2{2}/v3{2} approaches unity in the most central collisions, consistent with experiment. An exact response decomposition shows that residual fluctuations suppress the ratio through P3/P2 < 1, where P2 and P3 are Pearson response correlations for elliptic and triangular flow, respectively. This resolves the apparent flow hierarchy without requiring a breakdown of linear response or additional effects such as nuclear deformation.

items.title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
items.abstract: Designing a crystal for a target property requires choosing its elements, stoichiometry, and atomic structure together, yet gradients exist only for the continuous structural variables. We introduce differentiable Equiformer fast effective-atom theory (DEFEAT), which lets a pretrained EquiformerV3 foundation model accept continuous species weights and site occupancies without retraining on fractional data, thereby enabling gradient-based materials optimization. Gradients from fine-tuned property models and a machine-learned energy penalty then guide updates to composition, atom count, atomic positions, and lattice vectors in a single optimization. items.title: High-Volume Wurtzite MnSe in MnSe/CdSe Superlattices: Structure, Magnetism and Optical Response
items.abstract: Polymorphism in Mn-based chalcogenides offers access to magnetic semiconductors with distinct crystal symmetries, polar structures, and different magnetic orders. In particular, wurtzite MnSe exhibits an appealing interplay of electric polarization and several competing magnetic phases including altermagnetic order. However, stabilizing metastable polymorphs, such as wurtzite MnSe, in experimentally useful volumes remains challenging. Here, we show that a nanoscale-period MnSe/CdSe superlattice stabilizes wurtzite MnSe over micrometer-scale total thickness while suppressing the formation of the thermodynamically favored rock-salt phase. The increased magnetic volume enables bulk-sensitive characterization of this polar polymorph. items.title: Topology as a Design Variable: Joint Architecture-Sizing Optimization for SRAM
items.abstract: SRAM's power-performance-area-stability trade-off depends on bitcell topology, a discrete architectural choice that interacts non-separably with continuous transistor sizing. However, no open-source SRAM tool treats topology as an optimizable variable. OpenRAM generates SRAM layouts but performs no optimization, while OpenYield supports high-fidelity evaluation but restricts optimization to scalar sizing of a fixed 6T cell. OpenYieldV2 closes this gap through three integrated contributions. First, a fully parameterized compiler generates complete 6T and 10T SRAM macros with peripheral circuits and replica-bitline self-timing, enabling topology comparison under identical simulation conditions. Second, a few-shot TabPFN surrogate learns topology-dependent PPA responses with limited full-macro SPICE samples. items.title: A Neural Physics Solver for Richards Equation
items.abstract: A new approach to discretise and solve Richards equation based on the finite element method (FEM) is presented. The novelty of the approach, called the Neural Physics method, is that it expresses the discretisation as a convolution neural network (CNN) whose weights are predetermined by the integrals of the basis functions in the FEM. The Neural Physics method is physically consistent as it represents a discretisation of the governing equation and can run on CPUs, GPUs and the latest AI accelerators, resulting in an increase in computational speed. The Neural Physics method is demonstrated for two different discretisations of Richards equation, including a multigrid method that is realised through a U-Net architecture. The accuracy and speed of these methods is tested on a problem with a known analytical solution and compared to a standard FEM, and shows that the Neural Physics method is...

items.title: Strong phonon-coupled trion emission in Janus homobilayer
items.abstract: Janus transition metal dichalcogenides with broken mirror symmetry provide a novel platform for exploring many-body effects mediated by spin-valley-phonon interactions. Strong electron-phonon coupling demands a precise match between a strong effective dipole moment and nanometer-scale charge confinement. Here, we report thermally robust and enhanced trion emission in a symmetric bilayer WSeS with an S/S stacking configuration. The inward-pointing antiparallel built-in electric fields induce a strong electron confinement effect at the interface, driving dominant trion emission at cryogenic temperatures. Furthermore, a massive electron-phonon coupling strength (3.9) resonant with the optical phonon A_1^2 energy (51 meV) contributes to the thermal stability of this trion emission at elevated temperatures. By tailoring the interfacial architecture in Janus WSeS homobilayers, this study overc...

items.title: FoundaRF: A Physics-Informed Foundation Model Framework for Radio-Frequency Passive Components
items.abstract: Designing RF/mmWave passive components is a time-consuming process that relies heavily on expert knowledge and iterative EM simulations. Although recent ML surrogate models have shown great promise in accelerating passive design, they remain task-specific and lack generalization. This paper presents FoundaRF, a foundation model framework that unifies passive layout modeling across diverse layout structures and technologies. It combines a self-supervised encoder with adaptive layout processing and physics-aware decoders to enable few-shot transfer. Experiments across four semiconductor technologies show strong generalization to unseen structures, outperforming baselines with up to a 3.3x reduction in prediction error, reducing labeled-data requirements by up to fourfold, and substantially shortening design turnaround. FoundaRF establishes a scalable and data-efficient solution for RF/mmWa...

items.title: Deep-UV All-dielectric qBIC Metasurface for Refractive Index Sensing
items.abstract: All-dielectric metasurfaces supporting quasi-bound states in the continuum (qBICs) have emerged as powerful platforms for biosensing, yet their operation remains largely concentrated in the visible and near-infrared regimes. Extending these resonances into the deep-ultraviolet (DUV) to probe the intrinsic electronic absorption of biomolecules presents substantial material and nanofabrication challenges. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a hafnium dioxide (HfO$_{2}$) metasurface supporting DUV qBICs in the wavelength range from 225 nm to 340 nm with quality factors reaching 500. We further demonstrate its refractive index sensing capabilities through integration with a microfluidic cell and optical characterization in reflection mode. We show that the introduction of an aqueous buffer leads to a further quality factor enhancement. Achieving a sensitivity of up to approximately 60 nm/RIU...

items.title: Hybrid integration of a SESAM with a silicon nitride photonic integrated circuit
items.abstract: The realization of high-performance femtosecond lasers on photonic integrated circuits (PICs) requires robust, low-loss coupling between a saturable absorber and a photonic waveguide. In this work, we demonstrate the hybrid integration of a semiconductor saturable absorber mirror (SESAM) with a silicon nitride (SiN) PIC by micro-assembly. This micro-assembly strategy transfers the non-linear functionality of the absorber onto the PIC. We characterize the linear and non-linear performance of an unbonded SESAM and of a SESAM bonded to inverse-tapered SiN waveguides. At 1560~nm, the bonded device shows a waveguide-coupled modulation depth of 5.2\%, a maximum reflectivity of 37.2\%, and a saturation fluence of 47~\textmu J/cm$^2$. This work demonstrates that SESAMs can be integrated directly onto silicon nitride-based PIC platforms and provides a pathway towards fully integrated, self-starti...

items.title: Experimental demonstration of dual-polarization nonreciprocal thermal emission at moderate magnetic fields
items.abstract: Conventional thermal emitters obey Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which requires emissivity and absorptivity to be equal at each wavelength, angle, and polarization. This in turn places a fundamental limit on a range of radiative energy technologies as well as heat transfer. This constraint can however be overcome using magneto-optic semiconductors, which break Lorentz reciprocity under an applied magnetic field. However, in most prior experimental demonstrations, nonreciprocity has been restricted to TM polarization, since the electric field of TE-polarized light is parallel to the applied magnetic field. Here, we experimentally demonstrate nonreciprocal absorption in both polarizations at the same wavelengths and angles from a single structure, wherein a germanium Mie-resonant metasurface on a doped InAs layer scatters TE-polarized light into near fields with components perpendi...

items.title: Asymptotic-Preserving Tensor Neural Networks for 3D High-Field Kinetic Equations with Applications to Uncertainty Quantification
items.abstract: Kinetic equations in the high-field regime describe particle transport dominated by electric-field acceleration and collisional relaxation. These equations are widely used in simulations of plasmas and semiconductor devices. Typical models include the Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) and Boltzmann--Poisson systems. Their high dimensionality and multiscale nature pose two of the major challenges to accurate and efficient numerical solution. To address these challenges, we propose an asymptotic-preserving tensor neural network (APTNN) method. Specifically, to reduce high-dimensional computational costs and memory requirements, we adopt the canonical polyadic (CP) decomposition structure of TNNs to approximate their solutions. items.title: Dark-State Coherent Control of Excitons in TMD Monolayers: A Reduced Intravalley Lindblad Framework for WSe$_2$
items.abstract: Dark-state coherence in driven three-level systems underlies electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP). Their performance depends on the coupling topology: in a ladder ($Ξ$) scheme the coherence can bypass a lossy intermediate state, whereas in a $V$ scheme it is carried by two excited states that both decay. We develop a topology-resolved Lindblad framework for driven three-level excitonic manifolds at fixed center-of-mass momentum, in which a single exciton couples to phonons, the radiation field and a dilute exciton gas. The $Ξ$ and $V$ manifolds are selected from the exciton spectrum by systematically screening optical brightness, intra-excitonic dipole strength and state compactness, making the selection reproducible and transferable to other materials. items.title: FNO-Based Inverse Co-Design of Semiconducting Quantum-Dot Devices
items.abstract: Gate-defined semiconductor quantum dots are promising building blocks for scalable spin-based quantum processors, however their operational properties depend on several fabrication and control parameters, such as lithographic gate layout and applied voltages. Existing device architectures have been refined through repeated fabrication and experimental testing, producing layouts that support reliable device operation. However, this process does not exhaustively explore the design space, limiting the ability to obtain qubits with targeted properties. We address these challenges by presenting a differentiable inverse co-design framework for electrostatically defined quantum dots that jointly optimises gate voltages and the gate electrode layout. A semiclassical Thomas--Fermi electrostatic simulator provides reference data for a Fourier neural operator (FNO) surrogate, which predicts the two...

items.title: Micius-Flash: Lightweight Agentic Intelligence for Engineering
items.abstract: We introduce Micius-Flash, a 27-billion-parameter model for engineering with native multimodal input, deep reasoning and a 256K-token context window. We design the Micius data pipeline as a knowledge-tree-driven data flywheel comprising three stages: knowledge tree construction and expansion, data synthesis, and quality validation with hard-example augmentation. From this data, we train expert models for semiconductor knowledge and reasoning, hardware coding, and semiconductor multimodal understanding, along with agentic experts. Subsequently, we employ Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) to supervise training on sequences generated by Micius itself, thereby integrating the capabilities of these expert models into a unified model. items.title: Hall-Density Collapse as Direct Evidence for Percolative Conduction Onset in Monolayer MoS$_2$ Transistors
items.abstract: The origin of the apparent metal-insulator transition in two-dimensional electron systems remains debated. Using temperature-dependent transport and Hall measurements on industry-relevant MoS$_2$ monolayer FETs with amorphous HfO$_2$ dielectrics, we establish classical percolation as the underlying mechanism. We report two complementary signatures of disorder-driven conduction onset: a temperature-independent Hall-density collapse as a function of absolute gate voltage and a vanishing activation energy at a characteristic carrier density $n_{\mathrm{c}}$, identified as the percolation threshold. These findings identify dielectric-interface disorder, rather than channel quality alone, as the key parameter governing device turn-on. items.abstract: Near-Threshold Computing (NTC) offers a substan- tial energy savings, i.e., up to 10x, for digital circuits. However, due to Process, Voltage, and Temperature (PVT) variations, low voltage operating digital processors face increased susceptibility to timing errors. While conventional hardware based Timing Error Detection (TED) systems introduce substantial overhead, this work modifies MIMO algorithms to seamlessly integrate low overhead Algorithm Based Fault Tolerance (ABFT). items.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
items.abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. items.title: Photonic and Electronic Interaction of TMD-Hybridized ZnO Nanowire Lasers
items.abstract: Semiconductor nanowire lasers are promising on-chip coherent light sources for photonic integrated circuits, but integration inevitably places them in contact with other materials, thereby changing their properties upon hybridization. In this study, we examine the photonic and electronic coupling between single ZnO nanowire lasers and TMDs. Using deterministic nanomanipulation, we first hybridized the same nanowire first with a WS$_2$ monolayer and then with a MoS$_2$ monolayer. The respective lasing threshold rises, the emission is strongly quenched at high pump power densities, and the mode envelope blueshifts. Upon hybridization with bilayer, trilayer, and bulk MoS$_2$, lasing is fully suppressed. Finite-Difference Eigenmode simulations show that the TMD absorbs part of the evanescent field. items.title: Time-resolved infrared spectroscopy with entangled photons and visible-light detection
items.abstract: Time-resolved infrared (TR-IR) spectroscopy reveals molecular structural changes and charge-carrier dynamics on their intrinsic timescales, in photosynthesis, catalysis and optoelectronic materials, but requires complex sources of ultrashort infrared pulses, cryogenically cooled detectors to overcome thermal background, and intense probes that can perturb the sample. Quantum infrared spectroscopy avoids these constraints: harnessing quantum interference between the generation processes of frequency-entangled photon pairs, it reads out the infrared response of a sample by detecting only the visible partner photon, for which efficient detectors exist. To date, it has been limited to steady-state measurements. Here we demonstrate its ultrafast, time-resolved form with a picosecond visible pump pulse and a silicon detector. Each visible pulse generates photon pairs within a picosecond window...

items.title: DefectSkills: Guiding AI agents through first-principles calculations for point defects in semiconductors and insulators
items.abstract: First-principles defect calculations can now be performed autonomously by AI agents, enabled by established computational methods and open-source Python toolkits. However, reliable and repeatable defect calculations require clear scientific and technical guidance that helps agents resolve ambiguities and avoid errors in calculation setup, execution, postprocessing, and analysis. Here, we present DefectSkills, a set of structured prompts that provides human-in-the-loop guidance to AI agents performing first-principles calculations of point defects in semiconductors and insulators using the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP). The prompts encode human expertise and guide agents through unit-cell relaxation, electronic-structure and dielectric calculations, phase-stability and chemical-potential analysis, charged-defect supercell generation and calculations, finite-size corrections,...

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VII. Step kinetics
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the kinetics of attachment of new segments of the crystalline lattice (pyramids) at steps on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.

items.title: Electronic liquid crystals and superconductivity from doping a moiré Mott insulator
items.abstract: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moiré semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. Here we report the generic appearance of stripe phases in a doped moiré Mott insulator and the observation of a stripe to-superconductor quantum phase transition in twisted bilayer WSe2. items.title: PINND: Physics Informed Neural Networks for Solving the Drift-Diffusion Equations
items.abstract: The drift-diffusion equations are the fundamental building block for the modeling, design, and optimization of modern semiconductor devices. Solutions of the drift-diffusion equations rarely give way to analytical forms, and exhibit strong nonlinearity, with the solutions ranging over several orders of magnitude. These attributes have led to research into numerical solvers, and while many commercial Technology Computer Aided Design (TCAD) packages now exist, they may require long simulation times, exhibit sensitivity to initial guesses, and rely on mesh generation. Further, these solvers are not well suited for inverse problems where the design parameters of a device are retrieved from its desired functional characteristics. To address all these challenges, this work demonstrates the usage of Physics Informed Neural Networks for the Drift-diffusion (PINND) equations with errors comparabl...

items.title: HAWK: Heterogeneity-Aware KV Cache Transfer for Efficient GPU-NPU Phase-Disaggregated LLM Inference
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference exhibits distinct computational characteristics across its two phases: prefill is compute-intensive, whereas decode is more memory-bound. As a result, AI accelerators achieve varying levels of efficiency across the two phases. GPUs are well suited to prefill, but are often underutilized during decode. By contrast, NPUs can utilize their compute resources more effectively during decode. Motivated by this observation, we explore a heterogeneous architecture that integrates GPUs and NPUs, mapping prefill to GPUs and decode to NPUs to achieve high performance and efficiency. However, realizing such heterogeneous integration is challenging because LLM phase disaggregation requires KV cache transfer from prefill to decode (that is, from GPUs to NPUs), which is complicated by differences in inter-device communication mechanisms and KV cache tensor layouts.
